It's my pleasure. I love to talk about watches.

Ok, I know everyone around here is on the "buy what makes you happy" bandwagon, but you asked for advice.

The Citizen is descent and a good looking watch. If you HAD to buy one of the 3 I'd recommend that.

However, these are all chronographs and in the price range you are looking, I'd recommend you do not get a Chrono as it will have to be quartz as a mechanical would be way more expensive than that.

If you DO like quartz however feel free, but its a shame spending close to 500 for a quartz as you are being ripped off, because they are skinning cheap movements. (Lots of Quartz fan boys going to vote my comment down for this one).

Id recommend going for a good Day Date in your range, You'll find some awesome stuff. THIS SEIKO SNZH53 is very much in line with your style and its an amazing timepiece, I own one and am very very happy with it. Alternatively in the same range they have these, which look more sporty/elegant and less diver

Another diver at the higher end of your pricerange which is very, very, very good and quite well respected is a German brand called STEINHART don't get put of by the rolex homeage feel. Its not a knock off and while it has no chronograph it has a useful and quite cool GMT complication. If its not your style browse their site, all there watches are fantastic. If your hart is set on a chrono it may be worth forking out a little more for these guys as they at least have decent ETA movements in. (Again some snobs will hate me saying that)

Sticking with Divers a little longer The Orient Ray and Orient Mako are highly respected even if they are to big for me. Elegance wise these bambinos in white black and rose gold are awesome (those black and rose gold pictures on Amazon do not do the real thing justice.

It can go on for ages, and perhaps you are reading this laughing at me insisting you go for mechanical... but once you own a watch with that mesmerising sweeping seconds ihand nstead of the quartz tick, tick, tick it is hard not to fall in love with the magic and skill of a mechanical watch.

I don't laugh at anyone's passion and you seem to have it! I appreciate the time anyone takes to write out a well thought opinionated peace.

I'm looking more into mechanical watches overall and I can instantly tell what you mean when I watch videos of their movement. It's quite mesmerizing indeed!

Since someone else mentioned Orient I've taken quite a shine to them and the ones you suggest have caught my eye time and time again. I also like this Orient Automatic DB05001T and I've had a hard time finding it in stock in white but man do I love it!

Also those Seiko's are captivating as well.

Amazon is having a huge sell Wednesday and while I doubt any of the watches I am eyeballing will be for sale, I'm going to research the hell out of everything until then so thanks again for weighing in and giving me some options (especially the German Brand!)

So there could be a few things happening here. I haven't looked specifically at the Voat source code, but I've been working quite a bit with the beta API so I can somewhat infer how votes are processed.

After votes are sent to the server, they can have one of four status: NotProcessed, Success, Ignored, or Denied.

Since Voat has been under extremely heavy load, your votes are likely being initially registered as NotProcessed. There is probably a trigger on a set interval (possibly longer than you have currently waited) that then goes through in one big wave and processes all the votes that are currently of status NotProcessed. The query that gets how many upvotes you have given may not take the status of the vote into account.

The API docs say that a vote will be set to Ignored usually if it is a duplicate vote or a vote on a non-voteable item The API docs say that a vote will be set to Denied typically when the user doesn't have the necessary requirements to vote on an item.

Without seeing database information, this is all just guessing.

I guess it might be because of the processing load on the server. But I think there should be a fall-safe trigger to prevent this from happening. I mean some users might be experiencing this glitch but are unaware (since naturally you upvoat and then leave the page).
